title: Kernel fallback matrix and transient reservation for paged attention
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In high-concurrency multi-tenant workloads we observe tail latency spikes when paged-attention decode requests miss their preferred GPU kernel due to KV fragmentation or transient contention. Existing kernel selector picks the fastest kernel for steady-state but has no fine-grained policy for transient eviction/fallback and for reserving small transient KV segments for inflight prefill/decodes. This ticket experiments with a kernel fallback matrix coupled with a transient reservation window for hot prefill flows to reduce tail P95/P99 without regressing p50 cost-efficient kernels.

Goal: Define and implement a kernel fallback policy (matrix) that encodes compatibility/performance tradeoffs between kernel variants, and introduce a lightweight transient reservation layer for KV allocations during the prefill-decode handshake. Ensure the runtime can: 1) fall back to a compatible kernel quickly when ideal kernels are unavailable, 2) reserve short-lived KV slots for inflight prefill to avoid immediate eviction and decode thrashing, and 3) expose metrics and feature flags to safely rollout across Dedicated and Hosted clusters.
acceptance_criteria: P95 decode latency reduced by >= 15% on target mixed-batch workload compared to baseline without fallback matrix
No more than 3% increase in average token cost (p50) across same workload
Transient reservation avoids >70% of immediate post-prefill eviction incidents in the experiment cluster
Feature gates and runtime flags implemented for kernel-fallback and reservation with safe defaults
Automated unit and integration tests covering fallback decision paths and reservation reclaim behavior
Dashboard panels added for fallback events, reservation admits/evicts, and per-kernel queue lengths
design_notes: Introduce a kernel_fallback_matrix mapping: (model_variant, sequence_window, hw_characteristic) -> ordered kernel candidates with estimated degradation scores
Fallback decision must be fast (<100us) and stateless where possible; store compact per-model profiles in runtime config cache
Transient reservation is a short TTL lease attached to a KV segment; lease duration tuned to typical prefill-to-decode latency (default 250ms)
Reservation admission policy: allow reservation if (segment_free_ratio >= threshold) OR (request_priority == high) OR (recent-prefill-traffic to tenant > X), to avoid starvation
Reclaim policy: soft reclaim attempts first (signal requesting worker to use fallback kernel while background recompact runs), hard reclaim after TTL expiry or memory pressure
Compatibility: reservation must be optional on Private installs where KMS/audit constraints may block ephemeral metadata; expose flag runtime.enableTransientKVReservation
Fallback matrix will include kernel-level hints like: supports-prefill-copy, kv-alignment-sensitivity, decode-wave-granularity to avoid pathological choices
Telemetry: emit events kernel_fallback(reason, selected_kernel, preferred_kernel, latency_delta_est) and kv_reservation(event_type, tenant, segment_id, ttl_ms)
progress_updates: 2026-02-15: RFC drafted describing matrix schema and reservation semantics; reviewed by runtime leads (Aisha, Marcus, Li Wei)
2026-02-19: Prototype kernel_fallback_matrix implemented in staging runner; unit tests for simple matrix lookup added
2026-02-22: Simulation tests show fallback reduces 99th percentile in synthetic hotspot by 10% but increases p50 by 1.2% — need tuning
2026-02-25: Transient reservation PoC implemented: in-flight prefill path attaches short lease to segment; basic reclaim path added
2026-02-27: Early canary on staging cluster running mixed-batch public-chat workload; observed fewer immediate eviction loops for 3 tenants
2026-03-01: Decision to expose two feature flags (enableKernelFallbackMatrix, enableTransientReservation). Preparing PRs and dashboard queries for full experiment
test_plan: Unit tests for matrix lookup with corner cases (no compatible kernels, multiple equal-scored candidates)
Integration test: simulate concurrent prefill decode with KV fragmentation; assert reservation prevents immediate eviction for reserved segments
Load test: run mixed-tenant workload at 2x production QPS on staging; measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost delta
Chaos test: force kernel eviction and verify fallback path correctness and TTL-based reclaim behaves under pressure
Canary rollout: enable feature flags for 5% of production hosts with auto-rollback if p99 degradation > 10%
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal staging only; validate metrics and tests (runtime-1.24-staging)
Phase 1: Canary on Hosted small pool (5% hosts); monitor p50/p99, fallback events, eviction incidents (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Expand to Dedicated test tenants after manual sign-off; run billing impact analysis
Phase 3: Default on for non-critical tenants; opt-in for high-priority tenants until stable
Rollback: feature flags allow per-host disable; automatic rollback if p99 decode increases by >10% for >1hr
